content:
**Observations on test image:**
- Mango leaf, mostly green and intact
- Clear brown necrotic tip (apex necrosis)
- Small scattered brown spots/lesions along the leaf blade
- No white powder, no sooty coating, no gall protrusions, no margin erosion

**Comparing candidates:**

- **Anthracnose**: Reference shows green leaves with brown tip necrosis and scattered spots — bottom-right panel closely matches the test image (green leaf, brown tip, sparse spots)
- **Die_Back**: Leaves are almost entirely brown/desiccated — much more severe than test
- **Bacterial_Canker**: Distinctive serrated/eroded margins — not present in test
- **Powdery_Mildew**: White powdery patches — absent in test
- **Sooty_Mould**: Dark sooty/grey coating — absent in test
- **Cutting_Weevil**: Stems with cut petioles only — completely different symptom
- **Gall_Midge**: Dark raised galls along midrib — test shows flat spots, not raised galls, and has tip necrosis Gall_Midge doesn't show

The brown tip necrosis combined with scattered small necrotic spots on an otherwise green leaf is the hallmark presentation of **Anthracnose** on mango.
